title: TIMESTRETCH -- WSOLA granular time-stretch for live input or a loaded file

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: SOURCE menu: none (silent), live (input 1) or buffer (a loaded file).
LOAD: choose a sound file into the buffer. The waveform shows it.
Play / Loop: transport toggles for the loaded file.
TIME / PITCH: Stretch slows the sound down, 1x to 16x.
Grain: grain length, 5-200 ms. Pitch ct: pitch shift in cents (+/-2400).
Gain: output level, shown on the meter.
QUALITY: WSOLA sets how far each grain searches for a smooth join (0 = off).
Jitter: small random offset on grain starts. Sens: transient detection sensitivity.
Density: 2, 4 or 8 overlapping grains. More = smoother, more CPU.
Adaptive: shorter grains on transients (the Transient light shows them).
Extreme: Paulstretch-style smearing for very long stretches.
PRESETS: click a slot to recall, shift-click to store.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: A gen~ codebox records live input into a ~3 s ring buffer, or reads the file buffer directly.
Hann-windowed grains overlap and add. The read point moves at 1/Stretch speed.
Each new grain searches nearby for the best-matching start (WSOLA) to avoid phasing.
